metadata.title: Triad 01 frozen longitudinal relational behaviour graph
metadata.leakage_rule: No Episode 8 or Episode 9 response, retrospective explanation, outcome or formulation is included.
metadata.relationship_system: Established C–D partnership with D–E partnership and C–E metamour relation
metadata.methodology: Episode-coded nodes are immutable observations. Canonical nodes synthesise repeated person and system mechanisms and link to supporting evidence.
metadata.representation_rule: Retrieve typed person-level and relational-system mechanisms with linked episode evidence; do not expose a separate chronological memory stream.

nodes.speaker: Participant C
nodes.agent_text: Episode 2, Part 1: Participant C accepts a work opportunity that would bring Participant C to the shared city several additional days each week and assumes Participant D will welcome the increased proximity.
nodes.detail: Participant C accepts a work opportunity that would bring Participant C to the shared city several additional days each week and assumes Participant D will welcome the increased proximity.

nodes.speaker: Participant C
nodes.agent_text: Episode 2, Part 1: Participant C feels hurt when Participant D does not immediately welcome the opportunity as expected.
nodes.detail: Participant C feels hurt when Participant D does not immediately welcome the opportunity as expected.

nodes.speaker: Participant D
nodes.agent_text: Episode 2, Part 1: Participant D is excited about increased time together but protests that a decision with major effects on Participant D was presented through logistics and assumptions rather than joint discussion.
nodes.detail: Participant D is excited about increased time together but protests that a decision with major effects on Participant D was presented through logistics and assumptions rather than joint discussion.

nodes.speaker: Participant C
nodes.agent_text: Episode 2, Part 1: Participant C hears Participant D's complaint as contradictory to Participant D's repeated requests for more time together.
nodes.detail: Participant C hears Participant D's complaint as contradictory to Participant D's repeated requests for more time together.

nodes.speaker: Clinician
nodes.agent_text: Episode 2, Part 1: The clinician observes that Participants C and D are speaking from different injuries and each wants the other to recognise what hurt.
nodes.detail: The clinician observes that Participants C and D are speaking from different injuries and each wants the other to recognise what hurt.

nodes.speaker: Participant D
nodes.agent_text: Episode 2, Part 1: Participant D wants to determine who initiated the conflict; the clinician redirects from fault-finding toward understanding incompatible perspectives.
nodes.detail: Participant D wants to determine who initiated the conflict; the clinician redirects from fault-finding toward understanding incompatible perspectives.

nodes.speaker: Participant E
nodes.agent_text: Episode 2, Part 1: Participant E reports having little experience of what the relationship with Participant D would be like if Participant C lived locally more consistently.
nodes.detail: Participant E reports having little experience of what the relationship with Participant D would be like if Participant C lived locally more consistently.

nodes.speaker: Participant E
nodes.agent_text: Episode 2, Part 1: Participant E says time with Participant D has often depended on Participant C being away and that plans could disappear when Participant C returned.
nodes.detail: Participant E says time with Participant D has often depended on Participant C being away and that plans could disappear when Participant C returned.

nodes.speaker: Participant E
nodes.agent_text: Episode 2, Part 1: Participant E describes a scheduled meeting being delayed because Participant D chose additional time with Participant C, making Participant E feel secondary and unable to orient toward the future.
nodes.detail: Participant E describes a scheduled meeting being delayed because Participant D chose additional time with Participant C, making Participant E feel secondary and unable to orient toward the future.

nodes.speaker: Participant C
nodes.agent_text: Episode 2, Part 1: Participant C notes that the established pair changed their label from primary partners to anchor partners partly to avoid explicitly placing Participant E second.
nodes.detail: Participant C notes that the established pair changed their label from primary partners to anchor partners partly to avoid explicitly placing Participant E second.

nodes.speaker: Participant D
nodes.agent_text: Episode 2, Part 1: Participant D describes the relationships through non-hierarchical or relationship-anarchy values in which each relationship defines its own terms.
nodes.detail: Participant D describes the relationships through non-hierarchical or relationship-anarchy values in which each relationship defines its own terms.

nodes.speaker: Clinician
nodes.agent_text: Episode 2, Part 1: The clinician observes a tension between stated suspicion of hierarchy and practical differences in cohabitation, history, access and decision-making.
nodes.detail: The clinician observes a tension between stated suspicion of hierarchy and practical differences in cohabitation, history, access and decision-making.

nodes.speaker: Participant C
nodes.agent_text: Episode 3, Part 1: Participant C says an early conflict and a recent conflict shared the theme that Participant D experienced Participant C as less invested.
nodes.detail: Participant C says an early conflict and a recent conflict shared the theme that Participant D experienced Participant C as less invested.

nodes.speaker: Participant C
nodes.agent_text: Episode 3, Part 1: Participant C acknowledges not orienting toward Participant D in ways that made Participant D feel loved and prioritised.
nodes.detail: Participant C acknowledges not orienting toward Participant D in ways that made Participant D feel loved and prioritised.

nodes.speaker: Participant D
nodes.agent_text: Episode 3, Part 1: Participant D describes trying to be an exceptional partner while feeling below Participant C's work, performance practice and business commitments.
nodes.detail: Participant D describes trying to be an exceptional partner while feeling below Participant C's work, performance practice and business commitments.

nodes.speaker: Participant C
nodes.agent_text: Episode 3, Part 1: Participant C reports making deliberate efforts to prioritise time with Participant D and communicate love in ways Participant D recognises.
nodes.detail: Participant C reports making deliberate efforts to prioritise time with Participant D and communicate love in ways Participant D recognises.

nodes.speaker: Participant D
nodes.agent_text: Episode 3, Part 1: Participant D intentionally becomes less delicate and less enthusiastic so Participant C can experience something similar to Participant D's earlier hurt.
nodes.detail: Participant D intentionally becomes less delicate and less enthusiastic so Participant C can experience something similar to Participant D's earlier hurt.

nodes.speaker: Participant C
nodes.agent_text: Episode 3, Part 1: Participant C experiences Participant D's reduced care as a deliberate attempt to make Participant C hurt in the way Participant D hurt.
nodes.detail: Participant C experiences Participant D's reduced care as a deliberate attempt to make Participant C hurt in the way Participant D hurt.

nodes.speaker: Participant C
nodes.agent_text: Episode 3, Part 1: Participant C discloses crossing an agreed relationship boundary with a person who had been specifically excluded.
nodes.detail: Participant C discloses crossing an agreed relationship boundary with a person who had been specifically excluded.

nodes.speaker: Participant C
nodes.agent_text: Episode 3, Part 1: Participant C describes the boundary crossing as inconsistent with Participant C's own morals and accepts that it nearly destroyed the established relationship.
nodes.detail: Participant C describes the boundary crossing as inconsistent with Participant C's own morals and accepts that it nearly destroyed the established relationship.

nodes.speaker: Participant C
nodes.agent_text: Episode 3, Part 1: After the rupture, Participant C becomes more attentive in order to stop further harm and demonstrate that Participant D remains deeply important.
nodes.detail: After the rupture, Participant C becomes more attentive in order to stop further harm and demonstrate that Participant D remains deeply important.

nodes.speaker: Participant D
nodes.agent_text: Episode 3, Part 1: Participant D forgives Participant C and praises Participant C's bravery while continuing to organise later disagreements around the unresolved injury.
nodes.detail: Participant D forgives Participant C and praises Participant C's bravery while continuing to organise later disagreements around the unresolved injury.

nodes.speaker: Clinician
nodes.agent_text: Episode 3, Part 1: The clinician formulates Participant D as repeatedly approaching partners from an injured and neglected position, seeking recognition of being forgotten.
nodes.detail: The clinician formulates Participant D as repeatedly approaching partners from an injured and neglected position, seeking recognition of being forgotten.

nodes.speaker: Clinician
nodes.agent_text: Episode 3, Part 1: The clinician asks Participant D to contain powerful feelings long enough to perceive new information about partners rather than only litigating injury.
nodes.detail: The clinician asks Participant D to contain powerful feelings long enough to perceive new information about partners rather than only litigating injury.

nodes.speaker: Participant E
nodes.agent_text: Episode 4, Part 1: Participant E is invited to a family gathering but learns that the relationship with Participant D cannot be openly represented because Participant C has not disclosed non-monogamy to family.
nodes.detail: Participant E is invited to a family gathering but learns that the relationship with Participant D cannot be openly represented because Participant C has not disclosed non-monogamy to family.

nodes.speaker: Participant E
nodes.agent_text: Episode 4, Part 1: Participant E experiences concealment at the gathering and a later double-booking as evidence of being structurally secondary.
nodes.detail: Participant E experiences concealment at the gathering and a later double-booking as evidence of being structurally secondary.

nodes.speaker: Participant E
nodes.agent_text: Episode 4, Part 1: Participant E says uncertainty about status affects planning, security and the ability to imagine a future with Participant D.
nodes.detail: Participant E says uncertainty about status affects planning, security and the ability to imagine a future with Participant D.

nodes.speaker: Participant C
nodes.agent_text: Episode 4, Part 1: Participant C explains that after the boundary rupture, Participant D said Participant C had lost the right to determine the relationship's form.
nodes.detail: Participant C explains that after the boundary rupture, Participant D said Participant C had lost the right to determine the relationship's form.

nodes.speaker: Participant C
nodes.agent_text: Episode 4, Part 1: Participant C felt too insecure in the established relationship to advocate for the primary-style partnership Participant C still wanted internally.
nodes.detail: Participant C felt too insecure in the established relationship to advocate for the primary-style partnership Participant C still wanted internally.

nodes.speaker: Clinician
nodes.agent_text: Episode 4, Part 1: The clinician observes that central decisions are still commonly made by Participants C and D, while Participant E must ask for access or changes.
nodes.detail: The clinician observes that central decisions are still commonly made by Participants C and D, while Participant E must ask for access or changes.

nodes.speaker: Participant C
nodes.agent_text: Episode 4, Part 1: Participant C acknowledges that part of Participant C likes retaining some control over the relational system.
nodes.detail: Participant C acknowledges that part of Participant C likes retaining some control over the relational system.

nodes.speaker: Participant D
nodes.agent_text: Episode 4, Part 1: Participant D says the earlier boundary rupture makes Participant D want to give Participant C less control.
nodes.detail: Participant D says the earlier boundary rupture makes Participant D want to give Participant C less control.

nodes.speaker: Participant E
nodes.agent_text: Episode 4, Part 1: Participant E points out that Participant C remains a major decision-maker in Participant E's relationship with Participant D, including scheduling and family access.
nodes.detail: Participant E points out that Participant C remains a major decision-maker in Participant E's relationship with Participant D, including scheduling and family access.

nodes.speaker: Clinician
nodes.agent_text: Episode 4, Part 1: The clinician asks the established pair to recognise the difference between non-hierarchical language and Participant E's practical experience of unequal authority.
nodes.detail: The clinician asks the established pair to recognise the difference between non-hierarchical language and Participant E's practical experience of unequal authority.

nodes.speaker: Participant D
nodes.agent_text: Episode 5, Part 2: Participant D recounts a past public catastrophe followed by investigation, blame, legal exposure, family rejection and loss of friendships.
nodes.detail: Participant D recounts a past public catastrophe followed by investigation, blame, legal exposure, family rejection and loss of friendships.

nodes.speaker: Participant D
nodes.agent_text: Episode 5, Part 2: Participant D describes taking disproportionate responsibility to protect peers who faced additional vulnerability.
nodes.detail: Participant D describes taking disproportionate responsibility to protect peers who faced additional vulnerability.

nodes.speaker: Participant E
nodes.agent_text: Episode 5, Part 2: Participant E says this history helps explain Participant D's intense orientation around blame, accountability, loyalty and betrayal.
nodes.detail: Participant E says this history helps explain Participant D's intense orientation around blame, accountability, loyalty and betrayal.

nodes.speaker: Participant E
nodes.agent_text: Episode 5, Part 2: Participant E reports that Participant D can respond to relational injury with abrupt withdrawal, global statements and a sense that repair is impossible.
nodes.detail: Participant E reports that Participant D can respond to relational injury with abrupt withdrawal, global statements and a sense that repair is impossible.

nodes.speaker: Clinician
nodes.agent_text: Episode 5, Part 2: The clinician proposes that present transgressions can receive a larger package of fury carried from Participant D's earlier experience of being made a villain.
nodes.detail: The clinician proposes that present transgressions can receive a larger package of fury carried from Participant D's earlier experience of being made a villain.

nodes.speaker: Participant C
nodes.agent_text: Episode 5, Part 2: Participant C is present while Participant D's historical relationship to blame is connected to current relational intensity.
nodes.detail: Participant C is present while Participant D's historical relationship to blame is connected to current relational intensity.

nodes.speaker: Participant C
nodes.agent_text: Episode 6, Part 2: Participant C says that for roughly the first five or six years of the established relationship, Participant C never raised annoyances.
nodes.detail: Participant C says that for roughly the first five or six years of the established relationship, Participant C never raised annoyances.

nodes.speaker: Participant C
nodes.agent_text: Episode 6, Part 2: Participant C lacked confidence that Participant D could tolerate Participant C's complaints because the pair had not successfully worked through them.
nodes.detail: Participant C lacked confidence that Participant D could tolerate Participant C's complaints because the pair had not successfully worked through them.

nodes.speaker: Participant C
nodes.agent_text: Episode 6, Part 2: Participant C describes defaulting to easygoing behaviour and identifies adaptability as a coping mechanism.
nodes.detail: Participant C describes defaulting to easygoing behaviour and identifies adaptability as a coping mechanism.

nodes.speaker: Participant C
nodes.agent_text: Episode 6, Part 2: Participant C says Participant C performs mental gymnastics to remain agreeable and follow other people's schedules, interests or preferences.
nodes.detail: Participant C says Participant C performs mental gymnastics to remain agreeable and follow other people's schedules, interests or preferences.

nodes.speaker: Clinician
nodes.agent_text: Episode 6, Part 2: The clinician observes that distance, work travel and surface agreeableness allow Participant C to create relatively little overt conflict.
nodes.detail: The clinician observes that distance, work travel and surface agreeableness allow Participant C to create relatively little overt conflict.

nodes.speaker: Participant C
nodes.agent_text: Episode 6, Part 2: At a public event, Participant C avoids clear relationship labels and becomes less physically affectionate with Participant D when Participant E is present.
nodes.detail: At a public event, Participant C avoids clear relationship labels and becomes less physically affectionate with Participant D when Participant E is present.

nodes.speaker: Participant C
nodes.agent_text: Episode 6, Part 2: Participant C supports Participant D giving attention to Participant E but later notices the emotional toll and feels more distant from Participant D by the end of the day.
nodes.detail: Participant C supports Participant D giving attention to Participant E but later notices the emotional toll and feels more distant from Participant D by the end of the day.

nodes.speaker: Participant C
nodes.agent_text: Episode 6, Part 2: When Participant D asks whether Participant C can be flexible if boundaries are challenged, Participant C feels trapped because Participant C already struggles to advocate for personal needs.
nodes.detail: When Participant D asks whether Participant C can be flexible if boundaries are challenged, Participant C feels trapped because Participant C already struggles to advocate for personal needs.

nodes.speaker: Participant C
nodes.agent_text: Episode 6, Part 2: Participant C worries about living according to Participant D's ideas of what is right rather than identifying and expressing Participant C's own position.
nodes.detail: Participant C worries about living according to Participant D's ideas of what is right rather than identifying and expressing Participant C's own position.

nodes.speaker: Participant C
nodes.agent_text: Episode 6, Part 2: While describing disagreement, Participant C monitors Participant D's facial expression and fears having disappointed Participant D.
nodes.detail: While describing disagreement, Participant C monitors Participant D's facial expression and fears having disappointed Participant D.

nodes.speaker: Clinician
nodes.agent_text: Episode 6, Part 2: The clinician formulates Participant C as suppressing needs and experiencing ordinary disagreement as potentially displeasing or disappointing Participant D.
nodes.detail: The clinician formulates Participant C as suppressing needs and experiencing ordinary disagreement as potentially displeasing or disappointing Participant D.

nodes.speaker: Clinician
nodes.agent_text: Episode 6, Part 2: The clinician suggests that the system's idealism can make a direct no feel politically or relationally unacceptable.
nodes.detail: The clinician suggests that the system's idealism can make a direct no feel politically or relationally unacceptable.

nodes.speaker: Participant C
nodes.agent_text: Episode 6, Part 2: Participant C says Participant D's relationship with Participant E has become more significant than Participant C originally expected.
nodes.detail: Participant C says Participant D's relationship with Participant E has become more significant than Participant C originally expected.

nodes.speaker: Participant C
nodes.agent_text: Episode 6, Part 2: Participant C continues to support the arrangement while admitting that the increased significance is emotionally harder than anticipated.
nodes.detail: Participant C continues to support the arrangement while admitting that the increased significance is emotionally harder than anticipated.

nodes.speaker: Clinician
nodes.agent_text: Episode 6, Part 2: The clinician notes that both Participants C and E are beginning, in different ways, to state personal needs and limits within a system that finds this threatening.
nodes.detail: The clinician notes that both Participants C and E are beginning, in different ways, to state personal needs and limits within a system that finds this threatening.

nodes.agent_text: Participant C: Participant C often uses adaptability, agreeableness and accommodation to prevent overt conflict.
nodes.detail: Participant C: Participant C often uses adaptability, agreeableness and accommodation to prevent overt conflict.

nodes.agent_text: Participant C: Participant C can suppress needs or annoyance when expression might disappoint Participant D or destabilise the established relationship.
nodes.detail: Participant C: Participant C can suppress needs or annoyance when expression might disappoint Participant D or destabilise the established relationship.

nodes.agent_text: Participant C: Participant C may support an arrangement ideologically while discovering an unacknowledged emotional cost or need for specialness.
nodes.detail: Participant C: Participant C may support an arrangement ideologically while discovering an unacknowledged emotional cost or need for specialness.

nodes.agent_text: Participant C: Participant C monitors Participant D's reactions and can organise responses around avoiding displeasure rather than stating an independent position.
nodes.detail: Participant C: Participant C monitors Participant D's reactions and can organise responses around avoiding displeasure rather than stating an independent position.

nodes.agent_text: Participant C: Relational injury and reduced authority after a boundary rupture make Participant C's control, deference and insecurity coexist.
nodes.detail: Participant C: Relational injury and reduced authority after a boundary rupture make Participant C's control, deference and insecurity coexist.

nodes.agent_text: Participant C: Participant C increasingly notices the cost of receding and begins to identify needs that had previously been managed through flexibility.
nodes.detail: Participant C: Participant C increasingly notices the cost of receding and begins to identify needs that had previously been managed through flexibility.

nodes.agent_text: Participant D: Participant D is highly sensitive to neglect, blame and insufficient reciprocal investment.
nodes.detail: Participant D: Participant D is highly sensitive to neglect, blame and insufficient reciprocal investment.

nodes.agent_text: Participant D: Participant D can seek explicit accountability or determine who initiated conflict, making partners' perspectives harder to receive.
nodes.detail: Participant D: Participant D can seek explicit accountability or determine who initiated conflict, making partners' perspectives harder to receive.

nodes.agent_text: Participant D: Participant D endorses non-hierarchical ideals while retaining practical power within the established partnership.
nodes.detail: Participant D: Participant D endorses non-hierarchical ideals while retaining practical power within the established partnership.

nodes.agent_text: Participant E: Participant E experiences practical hierarchy through uncertain access, scheduling changes, concealment and limited decision rights.
nodes.detail: Participant E: Participant E experiences practical hierarchy through uncertain access, scheduling changes, concealment and limited decision rights.

nodes.agent_text: Participant E: Participant E wants enough clarity and dependable planning to orient toward a future with Participant D.
nodes.detail: Participant E: Participant E wants enough clarity and dependable planning to orient toward a future with Participant D.

nodes.agent_text: Relationship system: The established C–D partnership retains historical, domestic and decision-making advantages even when labels reject hierarchy.
nodes.detail: Relationship system: The established C–D partnership retains historical, domestic and decision-making advantages even when labels reject hierarchy.

nodes.agent_text: Relationship system: Participant C's accommodation and Participant E's uncertainty can reduce overt conflict while leaving unequal power unspoken.
nodes.detail: Relationship system: Participant C's accommodation and Participant E's uncertainty can reduce overt conflict while leaving unequal power unspoken.

nodes.agent_text: Relationship system: Stated non-hierarchical values can conflict with specialness, security, visibility and practical authority.
nodes.detail: Relationship system: Stated non-hierarchical values can conflict with specialness, security, visibility and practical authority.

nodes.agent_text: Relationship system: When one participant states a need, another participant may experience it as threat, disappointment or renewed evidence of neglect.
nodes.detail: Relationship system: When one participant states a need, another participant may experience it as threat, disappointment or renewed evidence of neglect.

nodes.agent_text: Relationship system: Clinician interventions repeatedly redirect from ideology, blame or logistics toward each participant's underlying experience and position.
nodes.detail: Relationship system: Clinician interventions repeatedly redirect from ideology, blame or logistics toward each participant's underlying experience and position.
